paper_title: A Bounded Parallel Intersection Type System
statement: Further work. Determining the precise complexity of inhabitation in the setting of system R remains an open and challenging problem. Addressing it would require resolving subtle combinatorial issues that arise from the interplay of bounded resources and vector-based type structures, making this a promising direction for future research.
context: An earlier system [7] imposes a similar dimensional restriction. We therefore provided a detailed comparison highlighting both conceptual similarities and key differences in expressiveness and technical treatment, throughout which demonstrating that system R offers a simpler and strictly more comprehensive framework that is easier to use in practice. Further work. Determining the precise complexity of inhabitation in the setting of system R remains an open and challenging problem. Addressing it would require resolving subtle combinatorial issues that arise from the interplay of bounded resources and vector-based type structures, making this a promising direction for future research. Another important avenue of investigation concerns type inference for system R. Since the system incorporates features of both set and multiset interpretations of types, it is not immediately clear whether the typability problem falls into NP or PSPACE, as established for related systems by Dudenhefner and Rehof [8]. Studying this question could provide deeper insight into the algorithmic behavior of the system. Similarly to system Rel of de Carvalho [6, Definition 4.1], it is interesting whether binary relations in system R can be related to term evaluation by means of a Krivine machine. As the system λCIL by Wells et al. [23] was also developed in the context of type inference problems, it would be interesting to compare it with the current system on the technical level. As the system Rel of de Carvalho uses relations in its models, it is interesting to see how the binary relations in the current system R fit into this kind of denotational semantics.
